architectures.title: MCP Runtime Security Gateway
architectures.best_for: Production MCP clients, third-party MCP servers, and tool execution flows
controls: Validate tool schemas and descriptors before registration
Pin trusted MCP servers and tool versions
Issue short-lived tool credentials per invocation
Run code/tools in sandbox with filesystem/network limits
Log every tool call, argument, result, and policy decision
open_gaps: No universal MCP security conformance suite yet

architectures.title: Agentic Red Team Evaluation Pipeline
architectures.best_for: Pre-production testing of agent workflows, tool misuse, goal drift, and prompt injection
controls: Run multi-turn adversarial scenarios
Validate goal and action drift
Test tool-output injection and RAG poisoning
Block promotion if ASR exceeds threshold
Archive results as release evidence
open_gaps: Multi-agent collusion and deception scoring remains immature

architectures.title: Enterprise Agent Governance Control Plane
architectures.best_for: Inventory, identity, policy, versioning, and lifecycle governance for enterprise agents
controls: Register agents with capability descriptors
Bind tokens to subject, audience, purpose, and duration
Review tool scopes and delegation policies
Enforce version expiration and retirement
Correlate policy evidence to NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / EU AI Act
open_gaps: Agent identity standards are still emerging across platforms

architectures.title: Secure Coding Agent Sandbox
architectures.best_for: Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and internal coding agents
controls: Prevent direct access to production secrets
Require review before config or CI changes
Block dangerous commands and unpinned package installs
Scan generated code and lockfiles
Keep immutable execution logs
open_gaps: Developer-experience friction can cause bypasses if controls are too strict
